note: Huitzil's PROCEDURAL BEAM STRIP (14z-71). The beam is a three-piece composite: a static muzzle, this stretching middle, and a static tip. The middle is a list-type 4 — a generator, not a coordinate list — and its handler COMPOSES ITS OWN BANK WORD (ori.w #$2000 at PRG:0x01B654 = bank 1) instead of taking the object's the way type 2 does (or.w $18(a6),d1). So the strip's art is fetched from gfx BANK 1, while our port relocated only the tenant's BANK-3 band into group C. Verified: our group-C 0x4EC0 equals vs2's bank-3 0x34EC0, the strip's art is vs2's bank-1 0x14EC0 (a different tile), and none of its tiles existed anywhere in group C. Symptom: right geometry, someone else's art — the maintainer's 'left half perfect, right half there but corrupted', reading as 'invisible' wherever the wrong tile is dark.
measured_by: 14z-71, from NATIVE's own OBJ records over replay 86 (all three variants, frames 3140-3830, every frame): pal 0x0C sprites whose y-word bank bits are 0x2000, expanded w*h. Base codes 0x4EC0/0x4EE0/0x4F10/0x4F90.
placement: group C bank 4 at code + shift. The shift is 16-aligned so the handler's within-row column wrap (base + row*0x10 + col) is preserved, and it is ALSO baked into the ported handler's code bias (vs2's 0x4200 + shift, addi.l in beam_list_type6.thunk_hex), which is why not one sprite list needs editing. RELOCATED 14z-83 (maintainer-approved): shift 0x1000 -> 0x3800, dst 0x86A0-0x87BF (head of ratified free pool 1) — the old dst 0x5EA0-0x5FBF sat inside PYRON's native band (vs2 group-B source, different bytes), the ONE real collision in the 3-tenant merged write set (tests/audit_gfx_merged_census.sh).
why_not_vsav_bank_1: Placing the art at these codes in vsav's OWN bank 1 would need no handler port at all, but measured: 160 of the 240 tiles in the span are real vsav art. Writing there would overwrite host content — a superset violation.
shapes_seen: widths 2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16 x heights 1 and 3 — the strip stretches as the beam extends
THE_BIAS: vsavj's type-4 handler biases codes by +0x3800; vs2's by +0x4200 — ONE byte apart at handler+0x7E, the only difference between the two routines. Our ported vs2 list data therefore addressed tiles 0x0A00 BELOW where native puts them, landing on the freeze/reflection art (maintainer identified it on sight). The ported handler carries vs2's bias PLUS the group-C shift: 0x4200 + 0x3800 = 0x7A00 (was 0x4200 + 0x1000 = 0x5200 before the 14z-83 relocation). Found only after the maintainer asked why a beam would not just repeat one tile — which sent me to look at the tile CONTENT (horizontal stripes, uniform left-to-right, 16 identical copies in ROM) and from there to the emitters. A single byte I had dismissed as 'a relocated address'.
span_rule: SPAN, not a sample (the 14z-70f grenade lesson). Sampling native's draws gave 0x4EC0-0x4F9F and missed the pal-05 strips at 0x4EB0/0x4ED0 — the build then drew those from uncopied positions. Copy every tile in the family's span instead; the extra copies are inert and group C has room.
